newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian business told to clean up image.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian business told to clean up image.

text.p: The head of Tanzania's Investment Promotion Centre (IPC) on Wednesday challenged the east African country's businessmen to clean up their negative image as cheats, tax evaders and price fixers.

"The truth of the matter is that government and the public in this country need to see clear steps being taken by the business community to rid itself of the unsavoury image that has unfortunately come to characterise private businessmen in Tanzania," said Samuel Sitta.
Sitta is the the director-general of the state-run IPC set up to help the once socialist country adjust from a command economy to a free market star.

"Whether we like it or not. Whether it is deserved or not, the sterotype of Tanzanian businessmen being looked upon as cheaters, tax evaders, price gougers etcetera is there," Sitta told a business convention in Dar es Salaam.

Most Tanzanians knew of cases involving phoney consultants and contractors or businessmen who had cheated commercial banks, he said. Dar es Salaam shopkeepers were not spared Sitta's wrath. They were accused of arrogance, rudeness and laziness.
"At the nuisance level are a lack of courtesy at many retail outlets. The attitude seems to be, the seller is king and not the customer," he said.
Sitta said Dar es Salaam enjoyed the "dubious distinction" of being a city whose commercial activity with the exception of street hawkers, closed down for lunch.
